title: Run report (yg check --json, and its --compact form)
$comment: This schema describes exactly what this release of Yggdrasil writes: every mapping is closed and every enumeration lists only the values this release uses. Use it to check a producer. Do not use it to reject a document you read: under the family rule a later release may add a field or a value within /1, and a /1 reader ignores what it does not know (see family-contracts).

stage.description: `log-gate`: components owe a justification entry; `structural`: a problem leaves the run unsafe.

issues.description: The findings that stopped the run, in the same shape as `issues`.

exit.description: `preview` on `yg check --approve --dry-run --json`: a cost preview always exits 0, so `code` is 0 whatever the tree holds; `reason` still says what the tree's own gate would say.

nodeOwned.description: Owned by a component's mapping. Null when the type-level tier is off.

typeCovered.description: Satisfied by an architecture type alone. Null when the type-level tier is off.

excluded.description: Excluded from coverage by design. Null when the type-level tier is off.

requiresNothing.description: True when nothing is required to be covered, so an uncovered file can never fail.

draftSkipped.description: How many rules stand at draft — each one's pairs are removed from the expected set entirely. A count of rules, not of pairs (it always was; the description said pairs until 6.1.0).

verdicts.description: Pair counts by what the lock says, summing to `pairs.length`. `unverified` counts the pairs no verdict was ever recorded for and `stale` those whose verdict was recorded over inputs that have since changed. The report and `issues` call both unverified (a `stale` one is an `unverified` finding with cause `stale`), so the unverified pairs are `unverified` + `stale`.

verified.description: Verified pairs split by reviewer kind, as the header reports them.

progressive.description: Null on a project that does not measure changes against a branch.

suggestedNext.description: The one concrete step the run points at, or null when there is nothing to do.

dryRunBudget.description: Present only on `yg check --approve --dry-run --json`: what the fill would cost, as numbers — the same counts the human budget header on stderr states.

groups.description: The text report's groups, in its order (added by the command layer).

next.description: The step `suggestedNext` names, as data (added by the command layer); null on a run with nothing to do.

banner.description: The text report's partial-result banner, or null: set when part of the graph did not load as written, so every other number here describes a fallback.

aborted.description: Present only when a recording run stopped at a gate (exit.status `aborted`).

notes.description: The text report's standing `note:` lines, in its order — facts that are not findings (added by the command layer).

compact.description: Present (true) only on `yg check --json --compact`: the same document with what a reader can recompute left out — `pairs` lists only the pairs that are not approved (`totals.verdicts.approved` still counts them all), an issue omits its `why` and `next` when its group (`groups[]`) states them, its `label` (its group's) and its `unitRef` (its `unit`, parsed), and the JSON is not indented. Every other field keeps its shape.

allowedRelations.description: On a `relation-undeclared-dependency` edge: the relation types the importing component may declare to `target` to sanction the import (`uses`, `calls`, `extends`, `implements` — only those the architecture allows between the two node types). Empty: the architecture forbids every such relation, so none can be declared — the dependency has to be removed, or the architecture changed with the user's approval. Absent on every other finding's edges.

subject.description: The block's heading sentence, as the text report prints it after `error[<label>]`.

cause.description: For an unverified block: why its pairs have no verdict.

why.description: The shared rationale, or null when the members' rationales differ.

next.description: The shared remedy, or null when the members' remedies differ.

cause.description: On an `unverified` finding (or its outside twin): why the pair has no valid verdict. `reviewer-missing`, `reviewer-unreachable`, `reviewer-failed`, `check-failed-to-run` and `suppress-marker-invalid` are infrastructure — re-running the same fill cannot clear them, and `next` names what does; the four fill-time ones appear on the report of the recording run that witnessed them. `stale`, `never-reviewed` and `deterministic-not-run` are pairs waiting for a fill.

label.description: The word a text report heads this finding with — `refused`, `unmapped`, `unverified`, or the code itself — the same word the text prints in `error[<label>]`.

unitRef.description: `unit` as a structured subject, the same shape as a pair's `unit`.

violations.description: A script rule's violations, one per reported location, never cut.

edges.description: The dependency edges a relation finding is about, never cut.

files.description: Every file a coverage finding names, never cut (its `what` may list fewer).

target.description: What the step is about: the node or file it names, when it names one.

cost.description: What running `command` costs — the whole command, never one block's share of it: every pending pair it would fill, advisory ones included. Script pairs are free; reviewer pairs are paid, and `reviewerCalls` is what they bill — each pair its tier's consensus — so the three numbers equal the `dryRunBudget` of `command --dry-run --json` on the same tree (`free` its `deterministic`, `reviewerCalls` its `reviewerCalls`). Zero for a step that is not a fill. A fill whose pending pairs are all script pairs is named as `yg check --approve --only-deterministic`, which cannot call the reviewer. (`reviewerCalls` added in 6.1.0.)

remaining.description: The errors the run leaves, each in exactly one bucket by what clears it: `needsFix` a code or graph fix, `fillable` pairs a recording run records, `needsUser` a decision only the user makes (configuring a reviewer), and `waitingOnReviewer` pairs no run can judge until a reviewer is configured or reachable. (`needsUser` and `waitingOnReviewer` added in 6.1.0.)

requiresUser.description: True when the step needs the user's approval before it runs: a decision that is the user's (configuring a reviewer sends code to that provider). Such a step is asked for, never run blindly, and its `command` is null. A paid fill is not one — an agent runs it once its change is final, and its price is in `cost`.

then.description: The step after this one, as the text report's `then:` line prints it, or null.

unit.description: The subject: one component, or one file governed by its architecture type.

node.description: The owning component, or null for a file no component owns.

kind.description: Which reviewer kind answers for this pair.

status.description: Effective status on this subject — what decides whether a finding blocks.

reviewer.description: Who answered: `deterministic` for a local check, the judge's name for a verdict recorded outside the configured reviewer, otherwise the reviewer tier the rule resolves to. Null when nothing has answered yet.

hash.description: The hash the recorded verdict is bound to, when the lock holds an entry at all.

filled.description: WHEN `--approve` filled this verdict, and at which commit — independent of whether the verdict is still in force, so a stale or refused pair still reports it. Null for a deterministic pair (filling one costs nothing, so there is nothing to attribute) and for any pair the lock has never filled. `sha` is null when no commit was resolvable at fill time (no repository, no commit yet, git missing from PATH) — the key is present regardless, so a consumer always finds it.

report.description: The violation report, on a refusal in force.

reference.description: The branch or ref the change was measured against.

changedInputs.description: How many changed paths the measurement accounted for.

outside.description: Enforced obligations held outside the change.

byteGuardKept.description: Findings the content guard kept blocking despite git reporting their files unchanged.

byteGuardUnavailable.description: The reference tree's object ids could not be reproduced, so no content check was made.

noiseFloor.description: The standing floor: advisory refusals, and enforced findings, on untouched code.
